expert.explanation: Abiatar having supported Adonijah was deposed (fulfilling the word against the house of Eli), and Zadok remained the sole high priest (1 Kings 2:26-35).

expert.question: Which scribe and minister of King Josiah presented the Book of the Law found in the Temple?
expert.explanation: Shaphan's family (notably his sons Ahikam, Gemariah and his grandson Gedaliah) later protected Jeremiah on several occasions.

expert.question: Which false prophet broke the wooden yoke on Jeremiah's neck and died within a year as Jeremiah predicted?
expert.explanation: Hananiah falsely announced the return of the exiles in two years; Jeremiah denounced his lie which gave false hope to the people.

expert.question: Which OT character is called 'much loved man' (ish hamoudot) by the angel Gabriel in apocalyptic visions?
expert.explanation: This affectionate title emphasizes Daniel's humility and constant piety in his old age in Babylon and Persia.

expert.question: Who was Zerubbabel in relation to David's royal line, and what promise did he receive in Haggai 2:23?
options: A Levite priest unrelated to David
A royal descendant of David (grandson of Jehoiachin), called by God 'my ring/seal', foreshadowing the Messiah
expert.explanation: Haggai 2:23 reverses the curse pronounced against Jehoiachin (Jeremiah 22:24) by restoring messianic hope in the line of Zerubbabel.

expert.question: What were the four main Jewish religious movements or groups at the time of Jesus?
expert.explanation: The Pharisees (oral tradition, resurrection), Sadducees (Temple aristocracy, denying the resurrection), Essenes (ascetic withdrawal) and Zealots (armed resistance) formed the landscape of the 1st century.

expert.question: What major doctrinal difference opposed the Pharisees and Sadducees, skillfully used by Paul before the Sanhedrin (Acts 23:6-8)?
options: The resurrection of the dead, the existence of angels and spirits — affirmed by the Pharisees but denied by the Sadducees
expert.explanation: By declaring 'It is because of the hope and the resurrection of the dead that I am under judgment', Paul immediately divided the congregation.

expert.question: Who was Hannah the prophetess in Luke 2:36-38?
options: An 84-year-old widow from the tribe of Asher who served God night and day in the Temple and praised God at the presentation of Jesus
expert.explanation: With Simeon, Anna represents the faithful remnant of Israel who awaited the deliverance of Jerusalem.

expert.question: What was the composition of the inner circle of the three disciples who witnessed the resurrection of Jairus' daughter, the Transfiguration and Gethsemane?
expert.explanation: Jesus particularly associated Peter, James and John at the key moments of his glory and his agony.

expert.question: Which apostle bore the Hebrew/Aramaic name 'Didymus' (twin) and expressed lucid courage before Lazarus ('Let us also go, that we may die with him')?
expert.explanation: Far from being just the 'unbeliever', Thomas showed courageous loyalty and made John's highest Christological confession (John 20:28).

expert.question: Which apostle asked Jesus the question: 'Lord, how is it that you will make yourself known to us, and not to the world?' (John 14:22)?
expert.explanation: This question allowed Jesus to clarify that his inner manifestation is linked to love and obedience to his Word (John 14:23).

expert.question: What is the portrait of Mary Magdalene (Mary Magdalene) according to the four Gospels (without confusing her with the anonymous sinner of Luke 7)?
options: A faithful disciple delivered from seven demons, who supported Jesus financially, remained at the foot of the cross and was the first witness to his resurrection
expert.explanation: The identification of Mary Magdalene with the sinner of Luke 7 or with Mary of Bethany comes from a late fusion without direct textual support.

expert.question: Who were Joanna (wife of Chuza, Herod's steward) and Susanna mentioned in Luke 8:1-3?
options: Healed women who followed Jesus and assisted him with their goods (patrons of the apostolic ministry)
expert.explanation: Luke emphasizes the determining spiritual and material role of the women disciples around Jesus and up to the empty tomb (Luke 24:10).

expert.question: Which companion of Paul's in Acts was first an eloquent Jew from Alexandria well versed in the Scriptures but knowing only the baptism of John?
expert.explanation: Priscilla and Aquila took him aside to teach him more exactly the way of God, making him a powerful evangelist in Achaia (Acts 18:24-28).

expert.question: In Paul's epistles, why is Priscilla (Prisca) often named before her husband Aquila (4 times out of 6)?
options: Probably because of his particularly active role in teaching or his higher social status in the Church which met in their home
Because she was an apostle of the Twelve
expert.explanation: This exemplary couple welcomed Paul in Corinth, trained Apollos in Ephesus, and risked their lives for Paul (Romans 16:3-5).

expert.question: Who was James 'the brother of the Lord' (Galatians 1:19), probable author of the epistle of James?
options: The brother (or half-brother) of Jesus, initially skeptical during his ministry, converted after an appearance of the Resurrected One (1 Cor 15:7) and became pillar of Jerusalem
expert.explanation: He actually presided over the Council of Jerusalem in Acts 15 and was nicknamed 'James the Just' in ancient Christian tradition.

expert.question: Who was Jude, the author of the Epistle of Jude (Jude 1:1)?
options: 'Servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James' — therefore also earthly brother of the Lord
expert.explanation: Out of humility, neither James nor Jude boast of being blood brothers of the Lord, presenting themselves first as his servants.

expert.question: Which collaborator of Greek origin accompanied Paul to Jerusalem, provoking a false rumor that he had introduced him into the forbidden court of the Temple?
expert.explanation: This false accusation by the Jews of Asia triggered the riot and the arrest of Paul at the Temple.

expert.question: Which Greek companion of Paul was not forced to be circumcised during the journey to Jerusalem in Galatians 2:3, proving the freedom of the gospel?
expert.explanation: Paul refused to give in on Titus (purely a pagan) to defend the principle of salvation without circumcision, while he later circumcised Timothy (son of a Jewish mother) out of missionary concern.

expert.question: Which character from Romans 16:22 served as Paul's secretary (amanuensis) in writing the epistle to the Romans?
options: Tertius ('I, Tertius, who wrote this letter, greet you in the Lord')
expert.explanation: Paul usually dictated his letters to a secretary before adding a few final lines in his own handwriting (Galatians 6:11; 1 Cor 16:21).

expert.question: Which NT character was a Jerusalem 'prophet' mentioned in Acts 15:32 with Judas Barsabbas to encourage Antioch?
expert.explanation: Judas Barsabbas and Silas, themselves prophets, exhorted the brothers of Antioch with numerous speeches after the council of Jerusalem.

expert.question: What is the name of the father of Alexander and Rufus who carried the cross of Jesus according to Mark 15:21?
expert.explanation: Mark's mention of Alexander and Rufus suggests that they had become well-known Christians in the receiving Church (perhaps Rufus in Romans 16:13).

expert.question: Which high priest ordered Paul to be struck on the mouth when he appeared before the Sanhedrin (Acts 23:2-5)?
expert.explanation: Paul called him a 'whitewashed wall' before apologizing out of respect for the office according to Exodus 22:28 as soon as he learned he was high priest.

expert.question: Which OT character is cited in Hebrews 11:31 as an example of heroic faith even though she was a pagan and a prostitute in Jericho?
expert.explanation: Rahab welcomed the spies through faith in the God of Israel, was saved with her family, and integrated into the genealogy of Christ (Matthew 1:5; James 2:25).

expert.question: What was the significance of Cornelius' conversion (Acts 10) in Church history?
options: The 'Pentecost of the Gentiles': the first uncircumcised pagan publicly receives the Holy Spirit and baptism under the ministry of Peter
The founding of the Church of Alexandria
expert.explanation: This episode broke down the barrier between Jews and Gentiles and forced the Church in Jerusalem to recognize that God also grants repentance to the nations (Acts 11:18).

expert.question: What professional speaker was hired by the high priest Ananias to accuse Paul before Governor Felix?
expert.explanation: Tertullus accused Paul of being a pest, a troublemaker and a leader of the Nazarene sect, accusations which Paul refuted point by point.

expert.question: What family bond united Berenice to King Herod Agrippa II during Paul's audience in Caesarea (Acts 25-26)?
options: His sister (Bérénice), daughter of Herod Agrippa I
expert.explanation: Agrippa II and his sister Berenice formed an influential but controversial royal couple to whom Paul testified about his conversion.

expert.question: Which disciple of Joppa, also called Tabitha, is the only character explicitly qualified as the feminine 'disciple' (mathêtria) in the NT?
expert.explanation: Acts 9:36 uses the feminine term 'mathêtria' for Tabitha, rich in good works and alms for widows.

expert.question: Who was Jason of Thessalonica mentioned in Acts 17:5-9?
options: The host of Paul and Silas who had to pay bail before the politarchs after the riot against the Gospel
expert.explanation: The rioters dragged Jason before the magistrates, shouting: 'These people who turned the world upside down have also come here!'

expert.question: Which synagogue ruler in Corinth believed in the Lord with all his household after Paul's arrival (Acts 18:8)?
options: Crispus (baptized by Paul himself according to 1 Cor 1:14)
expert.explanation: Crispus, head of the synagogue, converted with his house; Sosthenes was then beaten before the court of Gallion.

expert.question: Who was Gaius in the writings of Paul and John?
options: A generous host of Paul in Corinth (Romans 16:23) and/or the faithful recipient of the 3rd epistle of John
expert.explanation: Paul praises Gaius as 'my host and that of the whole Church', and John praises a Gaius for his walk in truth and his hospitality.

expert.question: Which faithful companion of Paul sent by the Philippians fell seriously ill to death in the service of the apostle?
expert.explanation: Paul sends him back to Philippi with the letter to allay their worry and to honor him for his dedication.

expert.question: Which Ephesian Christian diligently sought Paul in Rome without being ashamed of his chains and often refreshed him (2 Timothy 1:16-18)?
expert.explanation: While many in Asia had turned away from Paul, Onesiphorus demonstrated courageous loyalty to the end.

expert.question: Who were Hymenaeus and Philetus mentioned in 2 Timothy 2:17-18?
options: Two false teachers who deviated from the truth by claiming that 'the resurrection has already come', overturning the faith of many
expert.explanation: Their pre-Gnostic error spiritualized the resurrection and denied the future bodily resurrection.

expert.question: Which OT character is presented in Jude 9 in an argument with the devil over his body?
options: Moses (dispute between the archangel Michael and the devil)
expert.explanation: Jude points out that even the archangel Michael did not dare to pronounce an insulting judgment but said: 'May the Lord rebuke you!'

expert.question: Which NT prophet is mentioned as the author of Revelation and the 4th Gospel — but what unique characteristic does he have in his Gospel?
options: He signs his name in each chapter
He never addresses himself by his own first name, discreetly referring to himself as 'the disciple whom Jesus loved'
He was a Pharisee in Rome
expert.explanation: This literary discretion (John 13:23; 19:26; 21:20-24) puts all the light on Jesus alone.

expert.question: Who was Abigail in relation to the kings of Israel—and what theological lesson does her speech to David (1 Samuel 25:26-31) illustrate?
options: She encouraged David to take revenge quickly
She prevented David from shedding innocent blood by reminding him that the Lord would build his house and that his life would be kept in 'the bundle of the living'
expert.explanation: David blesses God for sending Abigail to meet him to restrain him from personal vengeance.

expert.question: Which king of Israel showed great repentance after Jonah's prophecy to Nineveh?
options: The King of Assyria (King of Nineveh)
expert.explanation: Hearing Jonah's preaching, the king of Nineveh came down from his throne, covered himself with sackcloth, and ordered a fast of repentance (Jonah 3:6-9).

expert.question: Which OT character is explicitly presented in the passage in 1 Samuel 9:9 explaining that the prophet was once called a 'seer'?
options: Samuel (the ancient term 'seer' referred to the prophet)
expert.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:9 explains a transition in terminology: 'He who is now called the prophet was formerly called the seer.'

expert.question: Which OT character prayed that the sun would stand over Gibeon and the moon over the Valley of Ayalon?
expert.explanation: The LORD heard a man's voice and fought for Israel on that one day.

expert.question: Who was Aaron in relation to the privileges and limitations of the old covenant priesthood according to Hebrews 5 and 7?
options: A mortal and weak high priest who had to offer sacrifices first for his own sins before those of the people—unlike the sinless Christ
expert.explanation: Hebrews 7:26-28 contrasts the weakness of the mortal priests of Aaron's line with the Son made perfect for eternity.

expert.question: Which NT character is described in Acts 13:1 among the prophets and teachers of Antioch as 'raised with Herod the tetrarch'?
expert.explanation: Acts 13:1 shows the remarkable social and geographic diversity of Antioch's leadership (from the aristocrat Manahem to the African Simeon Niger and Lucius of Cyrene).
